Phase 1: Verify where your project is

First, determine where your actual code lives.

Open:

C:\Users\ravil\.gemini\antigravity-ide

scratch
brain
knowledge
bin

Now open the scratch folder.

If inside scratch you see:

app/
components/
package.json
next.config.ts
public/

then your GitHub Clone project is inside scratch.

Phase 2: Decide what you actually want on GitHub

There are two possibilities.

Option A (Recommended)

Upload only your GitHub Clone project.

Repository:

GitHub-Clone

Contents:

app
components
hooks
lib
public
styles
package.json
README.md

This is the clean and professional approach.

Option B

Upload the entire Gemini workspace.

brain
knowledge
scratch
implicit
...

I don't recommend this because it contains Gemini's internal data, logs, and databases.

Phase 3 (Recommended): Start with a clean repository

This is what I recommend.

Delete the current GitHub repository contents and upload only your project.

Your repository should look like this:

GitHub-Clone
│
├── app
├── components
├── public
├── lib
├── hooks
├── styles
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json
├── next.config.ts
└── README.md

No:

brain
knowledge
implicit
conversation
.db
Phase 4: Remove nested Git

If your project is inside scratch, remove the nested Git repository.

Delete only:

scratch/.git

Do not delete:

scratch/

Only delete the hidden .git folder.

Phase 5: Create a new Git repository

Open terminal inside the actual project folder.

Example:

scratch

Run:

git init

Then:

git add .
git commit -m "Initial commit"
git branch -M main
git remote add origin https://github.com/lamberavi/GitHub-Clone.git
git push -u origin main

Now GitHub will show every file.

Phase 6: Organize the project

Your GitHub Clone should look like this:

GitHub-Clone
│
├── app
│   ├── dashboard
